title: How to Generate FBR QR Invoices in Pakistan (and Why They Fail)
metaDescription: A clear guide to generating valid FBR QR invoices in Pakistan — what the QR encodes, the step-by-step process, and the reasons QR codes fail to verify.
content:
What an FBR QR invoice really is

An FBR QR invoice is a normal sales invoice carrying a QR code that encodes the invoice reference issued by FBR IRIS. Scanning it lets anyone — a customer, an inspector — confirm on the FBR portal that the sale was actually reported. That is the whole point: the QR is proof of compliance, not decoration. A QR that does not resolve to a real IRIS record proves nothing.

How the process works, end to end

When you ring up a sale, your POS sends the invoice to FBR IRIS over its API. IRIS validates it and returns an invoice reference. Your POS encodes that reference into a QR code and prints it on the receipt. The customer can scan it and see the verified record on the FBR site. Each step has to succeed for the QR to be valid.

Generating a valid QR invoice, step by step

  1. Make the sale in an IRIS-integrated POS.
  2. The POS submits the invoice to FBR IRIS and waits for the reference.
  3. IRIS returns a unique invoice reference number.
  4. The POS encodes that reference into the QR code.
  5. Print or send the invoice with the QR — paper, WhatsApp, or SMS.
  6. Verify by scanning it yourself the first few times to confirm it resolves on the FBR portal.

Why QR codes fail to verify

The number one reason is that the submission to IRIS failed but the POS printed a receipt anyway — so the QR encodes a reference that does not exist. This happens when an authentication token expired, the connection dropped, or IRIS rate-limited the request at peak hours. The second reason is encoding the wrong reference. In both cases the receipt looks fine at the counter while the QR is hollow.

A real example

An electronics retailer in Rawalpindi printed QR receipts all day, unaware that its token had expired mid-morning. Customers who scanned the afternoon receipts got "invoice not found." Because the QR pointed at nothing, none of those sales had reached FBR — a silent gap worth a serious penalty had it not been caught during reconciliation.

How to make sure your QR invoices are real

Treat the IRIS dashboard as the source of truth: a sale is only reported if it appears there, regardless of what the receipt shows. Use a POS that refreshes its token automatically and retries failed submissions, and scan a few QR codes each day to confirm they verify. If yours are failing, our guide to common FBR POS issues and fixes walks through the exact causes.

faqs.question: What information does an FBR QR code actually contain?
faqs.answer: It encodes the invoice reference issued by FBR IRIS so anyone can verify, on the FBR portal, that the sale was genuinely reported. A QR that points to nothing in IRIS is just a picture — it proves no compliance.

faqs.question: Why does my QR code fail to validate on the FBR portal?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the invoice was never accepted by IRIS — a failed submission still prints a receipt locally — or the QR encodes the wrong reference. Confirm the invoice exists in your IRIS dashboard before trusting the QR.

faqs.question: Do I need a special printer to produce QR invoices?
faqs.answer: No. Any thermal or standard printer works, and you can even send the QR invoice over WhatsApp or SMS. The QR is data, not special hardware; what matters is that the underlying invoice reached FBR.

faqs.question: Can I generate FBR QR invoices without specialised POS hardware?
faqs.answer: Yes — a compliant POS app on a phone, tablet, or laptop can generate valid FBR QR invoices. The requirement is the IRIS integration, not expensive terminals.
